Something I didn't know for a long time and which I've been using a lot since learning is that if you create a bin directory in your home folder (~/bin) any files you put there will automatically be put into your PATH on your next shell login. This means that this automatically becomes your alias folder. Just make sure any scripts there are executable (chmod +x) and be happy!

Also I imagine some people don't know that you can replace the first line of your scripts with #!/usr/bin/python3 or some other interpreter. Your scripts will work just like BASH scripts but in your favorite language instead! The two tricks combined means you can easily create and deploy aliases and new console commands very quickly!

I mostly use Python for any script that needs some logic into it but for simple stuff (like what the article describes as an alias) using BASH with knowledge of how the $* $1 $2 etc variables work is also pretty good. If I even need a for loop though I'll use Python instead- I mean we're not in the 80s anymore and using BASH for that is pretty crazy unless you have a very good reason for it.

Hope some of you newbies can learn a trick or two from this comment :) hopefully something interesting for the veterans as well!
